primary.name: Evaluator
knows: Research data management concepts at a high level
does_not_know: RDF, triples, ontologies, or the semantic web
primary.goal: Assess whether DataStack fits their lab or institution — understand outputs and find the right entry point.
primary.key_gap: No technical background assumed. Needs concept-first explanations with real-world outcomes before any system detail.

secondary.name: Data Engineer
secondary.goal: Connect data sources, author mappings, and query transformation results.

narrative_arc.enters_knowing: They understand FAIR data in principle but do not know why semantics or linked data are the right approach.
narrative_arc.leaves_knowing: What linked data means in practice, why URIs and shared vocabularies solve the integration problem, how DataStack implements the semantic layer (Block 2), and what the ontology stack looks like from BFO to domain ontologies.
steps: The problem: data locked in proprietary formats — introduce without jargon, one paragraph
Linked data in one concept: resources get persistent URIs, meaning travels with the data
fig-linked-data.svg — the PMD stack as live example (CKAN → Fuseki → Sparklis → SPARQL)
The ontology stack — fig1-ontology-stack.svg with one-sentence explanation per layer (BFO → PMDCO → domain → application)
How DataStack fits: Block 2 of the semantic interoperability building blocks — fig5-building-blocks.svg with Block 2 highlighted
What FAIR means here: Findable (CKAN/DCAT catalog), Accessible (SPARQL endpoint), Interoperable (PMDCO-mapped RDF), Reusable (persistent URIs + open ontology)
Where to go next: callout box — three paths depending on reader role (deploy → P2 quickstart; map data → P3 author-a-mapping; explore outputs → P4 standalone-apis)

external_sources: semantics-industry-whitepaper/CONTEXT.md — core thesis and key messages

inline_assets_required.caption: Linked Data Foundation — knowledge artifacts linked by persistent URIs, queryable by any system
inline_assets_required.placement: after intro paragraph, before ontology stack

avoid: RDF syntax examples (turtle, JSON-LD snippets) — concepts only on this page

use: Analogies: ontology as structured dictionary, URI as permanent address
Real PMD examples: tensile test specimen, steel S355
